title: Invited: New Solutions on LLM Acceleration, Optimization, and Application
problem: Large Language Models face significant computational, storage, and energy challenges during training and deployment due to continuously growing model size and complexity.
motivation: Efficient LLM acceleration and optimization are critical to address the computational bottlenecks and energy consumption that limit practical deployment of these models.
method: The paper addresses LLM efficiency by improving four interconnected areas: speeding up the algorithms themselves, designing hardware specifically optimized for LLMs (called co-design), automatically translating code for custom accelerators using compilers, and using LLMs to verify that hardware designs work correctly before building them. By optimizing all layers together rather than separately, the approach reduces bottlenecks from algorithm design all the way through to hardware execution.
key_novelty: The paper's distinctive contribution is using LLMs to verify hardware designs work correctly (HLS functional verification), integrated with simultaneous optimization across algorithms, hardware co-design, and compiler techniques.
contributions: LLM-hardware co-design methodology for improved system efficiency
LLM-to-accelerator compilation framework for customized accelerators
LLM-aided design automation for HLS functional verification
limitations: Specific performance metrics, experimental results, and detailed technical methodologies are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: LLM acceleration through hardware co-design and compiler optimization
